data.name: Guide_Turnover_Overview

data.name: Guide_Turnover_Chart_ByMonth

data.name: Guide_Turnover_Chart_Tenure

data.name: Guide_Turnover_Chart_Reasons

data.name: Guide_Turnover_Chart_Trend

data.name: Guide_ActionCenter_Overview
data.value: This page is a company-wide worklist of stores that tripped one of the 7 detection signals (e.g. turnover above threshold, early-leaver spike) and got an Action Plan opened. Severity (Medium/High/Critical) is computed live from how many signals are on the plan, using cutoffs an Admin can configure on the Settings page — so it can change instantly if those cutoffs change. Each plan gets an automatic Target Resolution Date when it opens (90 days out, or 30 days if it's already Critical) and resolves on its own once its store stays clean for 2 consecutive evaluated periods. This page always reflects the current state of open/resolved plans — there's no period filter, since a plan's age and status matter more than which month it started in. See "How an Action Plan Is Created" below for the exact criteria.

data.name: Guide_ActionCenter_Chart_Reasons

data.name: Guide_ActionCenter_Chart_Region

data.name: Guide_ActionCenter_Chart_Trend

data.name: Guide_ActionCenter_Chart_StoresTable

data.name: Guide_ActionCenter_CriteriaTitle
data.value: How an Action Plan Is Created

data.name: Guide_ActionCenter_Chart_Criteria
data.value: An Action Plan opens automatically the first time any one of these 7 signals fires for a store with no plan already open, using that period's uploaded data: (1) High Overall Turnover — headcount of 5 or more and overall turnover rate at or above 15%; (2) Early Turnover (90 Days) — 3 or more hires in a non-provisional period and an early-leaver rate at or above 30%; (3) Low 6-Month Retention — 3 or more hires and 6-month retention below 70%; (4) Leadership Instability — 2 or more different Store Leaders recorded in the trailing 6 months; (5) Low Exit Sentiment — 2 or more exit interviews with positive sentiment below 50%; (6) Reason Concentration — 2 or more exit-interview reason responses where one reason is cited in 50% or more of them; (7) Early-Warning Watchlist — 2 or more currently active employees flagged high-risk. A generic "no dominant driver" note is added only alongside High Overall Turnover when none of the more specific signals above also fired. A new signal firing while a plan is already open is folded into that same plan rather than opening a second one — a store only ever has one Active plan at a time. Severity (Medium/High/Critical) is computed live from how many distinct signals are on the plan, against cutoffs an Admin can change on the Settings page (out of the box: Medium at 1 or more, High at 2 or more, Critical at 3 or more signals) — changing them instantly re-classifies every plan, open or past. The Target Resolution Date is set automatically the moment a plan opens — 90 days out, or 30 days if the plan is already Critical severity at that moment — and an Admin can still move it manually afterward; the quarter shown on a plan is only a reporting label based on its open date and has no effect on this date. In the background, every signal firing is also logged per store and period, and is marked "persistent" once it has occurred in at least 2 of the store's last 3 periods that actually had uploaded data (a period with no upload is skipped, never counted as clean) — this log supports future reporting and does not currently change whether or when a plan opens. An Active plan resolves automatically once its store shows zero signals for 2 consecutive evaluated periods.

See the Action Center page's guide for the full list of detection signals and how severity and target dates are determined.

data.name: Page_ActionPlanGuideSub
data.value: How an Action Plan is detected, created, monitored, and closed

data.name: APG_Overview
data.value: This guide explains, in plain business language, the full lifecycle of a Store Action Plan — how an issue is first detected, when it becomes an official plan, how severity and target dates are set, how progress is tracked month to month, and how a plan is eventually closed. It is a read-only reference and does not change any Action Center data or settings.

data.name: APG_S1_Purpose
data.value: An Action Plan is a formal, tracked response to a workforce problem at a specific store — high turnover, early attrition, leadership churn, poor exit sentiment, or a concentrated resignation reason. It gives the problem an owner, a severity, a target resolution date, and a place to record recommendations, notes, and progress until it is resolved.

data.name: APG_S1_Trigger
data.value: A plan does not need to be opened manually. The first time any one of the detection signals below fires for a store that does not already have an Active plan, a plan opens automatically using that period's uploaded data. A store only ever has one Active plan at a time — a new signal firing later is folded into that same open plan rather than starting a second one.

data.name: APG_S2_Body
data.value: Every Action Plan follows the same path, whether it closes quickly or runs for months:

data.name: APG_S2_Note
data.value: Persistence and Severity are evaluated continuously, even after a plan is created — they aren't a one-time check at the start.

data.name: APG_S3_Intro
data.value: Each period's uploaded data is checked against 7 detection signals, plus one fallback note. Any one of them is enough to open or update a plan.

data.name: APG_Signal_HighOverallTurnover_Desc
data.value: Headcount of 5 or more, and an overall turnover rate of 15% or higher. The broadest, headline signal.

data.name: APG_Signal_EarlyTurnover90D_Desc
data.value: 3 or more hires in a non-provisional period, with 30% or more of them leaving within their first 90 days. Points to an onboarding or early-fit problem.

data.name: APG_Signal_LowRetention6M_Desc
data.value: 3 or more hires, with fewer than 70% still employed at the 6-month mark. Points to a mid-tenure retention problem.

data.name: APG_Signal_LeadershipInstability_Desc
data.value: 2 or more different Store Leaders recorded in the trailing 6 months. Frequent leadership changes are strongly linked to team turnover.

data.name: APG_Signal_LowExitSentiment_Desc
data.value: 2 or more exit interviews, with fewer than 50% reflecting positive sentiment. Signals a culture or management concern surfacing at exit.

data.name: APG_Signal_ReasonConcentration_Desc
data.value: 2 or more exit-interview reason responses, with a single reason cited in 50% or more of them — for example, most departures citing pay or scheduling.

data.name: APG_Signal_EarlyWarningWatchlist_Desc
data.value: 2 or more currently active employees flagged high-risk on the Early Warning watchlist — a forward-looking signal based on staff still employed, not past exits.

data.name: APG_Signal_NoDominantDriver_Desc
data.value: Not an independent signal. Added only alongside High Overall Turnover when none of the more specific signals above also fired — an honest note that no single root cause stands out yet.

data.name: APG_S4_Body
data.value: For normal, non-critical issues, a signal is only treated as persistent once it has fired in at least 2 of the store's last 3 evaluation periods that actually have uploaded data. A period with no upload is not counted as a healthy or clean period — it is simply excluded, so a store can't look artificially stable just because a period was skipped.

data.name: APG_S4_Critical
data.value: Critical-severity issues bypass this normal persistence requirement — they are acted on immediately rather than waiting to reappear across periods, given the urgency they represent.

data.name: APG_Severity_MediumDesc
data.value: One distinct signal detected on the plan.

data.name: APG_Severity_HighDesc
data.value: Two distinct signals detected on the plan at the same time.

data.name: APG_Severity_CriticalDesc
data.value: Three or more distinct signals detected on the plan at the same time — the most urgent tier.

data.name: APG_Severity_Body
data.value: Severity isn't fixed when a plan is created — it is computed live from how many distinct signals are currently active on that plan.

data.name: APG_Severity_ConfigNote
data.value: The signal-count cutoffs for Medium, High, and Critical are configurable by an Admin on the Action Plan Severity settings page. Changing them re-classifies every plan — open or already resolved — instantly, and can also affect the target resolution window below.

data.name: APG_S6_Standard
data.value: Standard Action Plan — the target resolution date is set 90 days from the day the plan opens.

data.name: APG_S6_Critical
data.value: Critical / Immediate Action Plan — if the plan is already Critical severity the moment it opens, the target resolution date is set 30 days from the day it opens instead.

data.name: APG_S6_Quarter
data.value: The Reporting Quarter shown on a plan is only a classification label based on when the plan opened, used for reporting and grouping. It is separate from the target resolution date and does not extend or shorten the resolution deadline.

data.name: APG_S7_Title
data.value: Inside an Action Plan (Store Action Center Details)

data.name: APG_Inside_Kpi
data.value: KPI / Baseline vs. Latest — the store's Turnover Rate, Early Leaver (90-Day) Rate, and Retention Rate as they stood when the plan opened, compared with the latest recorded values, so progress is visible at a glance.

data.name: APG_Inside_Monthly
data.value: Monthly Performance — every recorded monthly snapshot since the plan opened, showing Turnover %, Early-Leaver %, Retention %, signal count, and the change in Turnover % versus the previous month.

data.name: APG_Inside_Signals
data.value: Signal History — which signals fired in each period the store has uploaded data for, and whether each has become persistent.

data.name: APG_Inside_Recs
data.value: Recommendations — suggested actions tailored to the specific signals detected, grouped by category (e.g. Onboarding, Retention, Leadership), which can be checked off as they're completed.

data.name: APG_Inside_Notes
data.value: Actions / Notes — a running log where the responsible person records what was done and when.

data.name: APG_Inside_Target
data.value: Target Resolution Date — the 90- or 30-day deadline described above, shown alongside the plan's current age.

data.name: APG_Inside_Streak
data.value: Healthy Streak — how many consecutive clean evaluation periods the store has had since the plan opened, out of the 2 needed for automatic resolution.

data.name: APG_Inside_Closure
data.value: Closure / Outcome — once resolved, the plan shows how and when it closed, who closed it (if closed manually), and the recorded closing reason.

data.name: APG_S8_Body
data.value: While a plan is open, its store keeps being evaluated every time new monthly data is uploaded — this is what drives the Monthly Performance table and the Healthy Streak. The metrics tracked each month are:

data.name: APG_Monitoring_Turnover
data.value: The store's turnover rate for that month.

data.name: APG_Monitoring_EarlyLeaver
data.value: The 90-day early-leaver rate for that month.

data.name: APG_Monitoring_Retention
data.value: The 6-month retention rate for that month.

data.name: APG_Monitoring_SignalCount
data.value: How many of the 7 detection signals were active that month.

data.name: APG_Monitoring_Change
data.value: The change in turnover rate compared with the previous month, so a trend is visible without checking every prior row.

data.name: APG_S9_Body1
data.value: A month with zero active signals counts as a healthy period and adds to the plan's Healthy Streak. A healthy streak is good evidence that the underlying issue is improving.

data.name: APG_S9_Body2
data.value: Reaching 2 consecutive healthy periods triggers automatic resolution — but any signal firing again resets the streak to zero. Short of that automatic threshold, a healthy streak on its own does not close a plan; closing it early still requires a deliberate review and decision.

data.name: APG_S10_Auto
data.value: Automatic Resolution — a plan resolves on its own once its store shows zero active signals for 2 consecutive evaluated periods.

data.name: APG_S10_Manual
data.value: Manual Closure — an Admin can close a plan before that point, recording who closed it and a written reason. This should only be used when the issue was genuinely addressed outside the normal detection cycle.

data.name: APG_S10_OutcomesIntro
data.value: In practice, the recorded closing reason documents one of these outcomes:

data.name: APG_Outcome_Resolved
data.value: Resolved — the issue was fully addressed; metrics returned to a healthy range.

data.name: APG_Outcome_PartiallyImproved
data.value: Partially Improved — meaningful progress was made, but the issue was not fully resolved.

data.name: APG_Outcome_NotImproved
data.value: Not Improved — little or no change since the plan opened.

data.name: APG_Outcome_Escalated
data.value: Escalated — the issue proved more serious than initially detected and was raised for additional attention beyond the plan itself.

data.name: APG_S11_Continuing
data.value: If the underlying issue is still unresolved when a quarter ends, the same Action Plan simply continues into the next quarter — its target date, severity, and history carry forward unchanged. Crossing a quarter boundary is not, by itself, a sign of anything unusual, and it does not make the plan Chronic or Recurring.

data.name: APG_S11_Chronic
data.value: Chronic / Recurring describes a different situation: a store whose Action Plan was genuinely resolved — closed, automatically or manually — and later needed a new plan opened because the same or a related problem came back. The Action Center flags these as "Repeat Problem Stores" and highlights them for a deeper root-cause review, since the earlier fix didn't hold.

data.name: APG_Example_Step1
data.value: Signal — Store #482 uploads its monthly data. Its 90-day early-leaver rate is 34%, above the 30% threshold, so Early Turnover (90 Days) fires.

data.name: APG_Example_Step2
data.value: Persistence — The same signal had already fired in the prior period. That's 2 of the last 3 periods with data, so it's marked persistent.

data.name: APG_Example_Step3
data.value: Plan Creation — No plan was open for Store #482, so an Action Plan opens automatically, carrying this one detected signal.

data.name: APG_Example_Step4
data.value: Severity — With 1 distinct signal active, the plan is classified Medium under the default cutoffs.

data.name: APG_Example_Step5
data.value: Target Date — Because the plan is Medium, not Critical, at creation, its target resolution date is set 90 days out.

data.name: APG_Example_Step6
data.value: Monthly Progress — Over the next two monthly uploads, the Store Leader follows the onboarding recommendations. The early-leaver rate drops to 22%, then 18% — both below threshold, so the signal stops firing.

data.name: APG_Example_Step7
data.value: Healthy Streak — Those two clean months in a row complete the 2-period healthy streak.

data.name: APG_Example_Step8
data.value: Review & Outcome — The plan auto-resolves with outcome Resolved. If the same store spikes again months later, a brand-new plan opens and, since this store now has more than one plan on record, it's flagged as a Repeat Problem Store — not because it merely crossed a quarter, but because the earlier plan had already been closed.
